standard.title: Contribute to discussions with diverse views
standard.description: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare cultural experiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can collaborate using transacting, negotiating and justifying language to plan events (AC9LCH8C02). They have conducted community interviews and planned community-facing events. They have not yet organised authentic cultural experiences for school or community contexts, contributed to collaborative digital platforms, or collected and analysed community data for presentations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students contribute to discussions involving diverse views — negotiating outcomes, addressing issues, and comparing cultural experiences — including through collaborative digital platforms and community-facing cultural events.

nodes.label: Negotiating outcomes with diverse views
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can contribute productively to discussions where diverse views must be negotiated — managing disagreement, incorporating different perspectives, and working toward a shared outcome.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to a discussion with diverse perspectives, using at least two negotiation strategies (acknowledging a different view, finding common ground, or proposing a compromise) to work toward an outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in discussions involving diverse cultural experiences and views; manage disagreements productively; incorporate different perspectives into planning; negotiate outcomes that address competing interests; promote inclusive approaches to community activities.
wider: Lead a discussion where views conflict — facilitate productive negotiation and bring the group to a shared outcome using target language

Compare negotiation strategies across cultural contexts — identify how the target language community manages disagreement differently from Australian contexts and discuss implications for intercultural collaboration
nodes.hinge_reason: Negotiating diverse views is the core demand of this descriptor and the prerequisite for all community-facing collaborative activity. Students who can only interact with like-minded partners cannot manage the genuine diversity of perspectives that real community and cultural engagement requires.

response_modes.reason: Productive negotiation with diverse views requires students to understand others' positions before responding — a listening-first, reasoning-second discipline. Explicit negotiation strategy instruction followed by practice in genuinely diverse discussion contexts builds this capacity.

success_criteria: Uses at least two negotiation strategies during a discussion with diverse perspectives
Works toward a shared outcome without abandoning the target language

nodes.label: Collaborative digital platforms and peer feedback
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can contribute to collaborative digital platforms — blogs, vlogs, shared presentations — evaluating peers' contributions and providing justified feedback.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute at least one substantive post or entry to a collaborative digital platform and provide justified feedback on at least one peer's contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Create and contribute to collaborative blogs about language learning; evaluate peers' contributions using metalanguage; create multimodal resources for Chinese learners at various levels; collect and present community data; use digital tools for collaborative planning and publication.
wider: Create a vlog or digital resource for a specific target audience — evaluate its effectiveness with that audience and revise based on feedback
Collect, analyse and present community data on a cultural topic — comparing findings across different community groups and discussing what the comparison reveals

response_modes.reason: Digital collaborative platforms require students to manage different roles — contributor, editor, commentator — across varied platform types. Practice across different digital contexts builds the flexible digital collaboration skills the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital platform contributions can reach real target language audiences beyond the classroom — a uniquely authentic communicative context for background learners. Width investment here creates the highest-authenticity conditions for target language use at this level.
success_criteria: Contributes a substantive entry to a collaborative digital platform
Provides justified feedback on at least one peer's contribution using specific criteria

nodes.label: Organising community cultural experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can organise authentic cultural experiences for school or community audiences — planning, promoting, executing and evaluating the event using target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to organising a cultural experience for a school or community audience, participating in at least three planning decisions in target language and producing at least one promotional or informational material.
nodes.typical_width: Organise authentic cultural experiences for school or local community — cultural events, excursions, community-facing activities; create promotional materials; collaborate with target language community peers; reflect on and evaluate the experience.
wider: Lead the organisation of a community cultural event — coordinate all planning, promotion, execution and evaluation using target language, with real community participants
Evaluate the cultural event from multiple perspectives — participant, organiser, cultural community member — and synthesise these perspectives into a reflective account

response_modes.reason: Community event organisation integrates diverse-view negotiation (node 1) and digital collaboration (node 2) into a full real-stakes project. The teaching investment is in genuine community connections — real cultural events, real community participants — that require all collaborative and communicative skills simultaneously.

success_criteria: Contributes to organising a community cultural experience with at least three target language planning decisions
Produces at least one promotional or informational material for the event
